findings.text: The live operator flag file documents SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED, which exists nowhere else and disables nothing
findings.detail: Canonical name is OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED; aliases are OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED, MK_GOAL_DISABLED, MK_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED. SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED is in neither list and appears exactly once in the repository. Every neighbouring line in the live file uses the SYSTEM_<CONCERN>_DISABLED shape, which genuinely works for dispatch (hook-flags.cjs:53), so the one line that breaks the pattern is the one that does nothing. The file is gitignored, so no test can catch it.

findings.text: The PLUGIN_DISABLED error names the alias, not the switch that fired
findings.detail: DISABLED_ENV is OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED and is interpolated into eleven guard messages, but every guard calls isPluginDisabled() which reads OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED first. Setting the canonical flag produces a message naming a different variable.

findings.text: The kill switch also switches off the session-free reads and the aggregate diagnostics
findings.detail: The CLI returns PLUGIN_DISABLED before routing, so packet, packet-log, doctor and health all fail while disabled, though the docs describe them as session-free and read-only. Meanwhile the library functions appendPacketLog (goal-core.cjs:1113) and describePacketGoal (goal-core.cjs:1042) carry no disable check, so a direct importer still writes rows that the CLI refuses to write.

findings.text: The hook enforces the durable budget on the packets the contract excludes
findings.detail: The manifest says appliesTo is phase parents and top-level packets, with phase children unbounded. resolveGoalBudget reads only warnChars and errorChars and drops appliesTo; budgetState compares every packet; the CLI emits warning= for a phase child that is over. Re-tested in ring 3 against the validator's own resolver.

findings.text: Injection-only does not mean read-only: both injection-only adapters mutate the record
findings.detail: Cursor and Devin both import recordTurn and bump turnsUsed, revision, updatedAtMs and lastActivityAtMs. goal-plugin.md states this precisely; README.md's injection-only framing does not.

findings.text: The manage CLI and the OpenCode plugin do not expose the same status field names
findings.detail: The plugin contract names tokens_used and usage_source as canonical, with budget-prefixed aliases. The CLI emits usage_source but never tokens_used, so a script reading the canonical field works against one surface and silently gets nothing from the other.

findings.text: resolveWorkspaceRoot is a byte-for-byte twin of resolveRepoRoot and has no consumer
findings.detail: Same markers, same depth loop, same fallback. The core calls its own resolveRepoRoot at four sites; resolveWorkspaceRoot is referenced only by its definition, its export and one test. goal-slice.cjs has three importers: goal-core.cjs, opencode-goal.js and its own test.

findings.text: README section 6 omits OPENCODE_GOAL_RUNTIME_LABEL, and its name collides conceptually with --runtime
findings.detail: The CLI reads the label; the repo-root example env documents it; the engine README does not. --runtime is constrained to lowercase and forms the state key, while the label is a free-form display string carrying values like Pi and Cursor.

findings.text: The append gateway could not be used inside a contained lineage
findings.detail: append-mode-event.cjs writes the state log and receipts under the spec folder, outside this lineage's bound write surface. Records are appended in-lineage in the same field shape instead. Recorded as a deviation in every iteration file and in research.md.

findings.text: Two live implementations of the workspace-root walk, in the two implementations that claim to share one boundary
findings.detail: goal-slice.cjs states it exists so the CommonJS core and the ESM plugin cannot drift apart on the boundary. That holds for the frontmatter boundary it introduces. The workspace root, which decides which .opencode/skills tree the state dir lives under, is a second boundary drawn twice, and the two implementations take different sides.

findings.text: OPENCODE_GOAL_STATE_DIR isolates state on four runtimes and is ignored by OpenCode, which writes to the real state root
findings.detail: The core reads the env override between an explicit option and the repo-root default. The plugin reads an explicit option then a constant derived from its own file location, and the literal appears nowhere in it. README:180 tells operators to use temporary state-dir paths for manual probes precisely so they never touch the live tree; on OpenCode that instruction is wrong.

findings.text: The plugin repeats the wrong-variable disable message
findings.detail: Same shape as R1-F2 in the second implementation: DISABLED_ENV names the alias, the gate reads the canonical flag first.

findings.text: Disabling the goal hook disables the goal diagnostics on both front ends
findings.detail: Ring 1 found this in the CLI and suspected a quirk. The plugin does the same: the disable check precedes history, doctor, health and packet. Two independent front ends make it a contract: the switch that stops goal behaviour also stops the reporting that would explain what it stopped.

findings.text: The injection contract's verbatim Role line enumerates Cursor and Pi but not Devin
findings.detail: The same section names Devin as an owner and documents its channel, and the adapter renders RuntimeLabel Devin. A reader copying the published block shape gets the wrong one for the adapter whose payload envelope differs most.

findings.text: The Cursor hook README calls the goal hook Cursor-only while a Devin twin is registry-bound twice
findings.detail: True of the file in the directory it describes, false as a fleet statement, and contradicted one directory over.

findings.text: Three of the four runtime symlinks are decoration; only Pi's is a discovery path
findings.detail: The generated registries invoke .opencode/hooks/goal/{cursor,devin}/goal-inject.mjs directly. .cursor/hooks/goal-inject.mjs and .devin/hooks/goal-inject.mjs resolve and are never executed; .opencode/hooks/goal/opencode/opencode-goal.js is documented as browsability-only. Pi is the exception: .pi/extensions/goal-context.ts is what Pi's loader discovers.

findings.text: Claude and Codex goal support is asserted in two documents and carried by nothing in this repository
findings.detail: No Claude goal command, no Codex goal prompt, no goal binding for either runtime in the hook registry, and no test that would fail if the host command changed. The claim is about software outside this tree. UNKNOWN whether those products currently ship the assumed surface; their own documentation would settle it.

findings.text: The plugin command surface is the third place to present the disable alias as the primary name
findings.detail: The alias does work, so the instruction is not wrong; but nothing on any of the three surfaces says which name the resolver reads first.

findings.text: The durable budget applies to phase children in the goal engine and to nobody else; a phase child passes validate.sh --strict and is then reported as past the error tier
findings.detail: Six surfaces scope the budget to phase parents and top-level packets: the manifest declares appliesTo, the validator computes budgetApplies from level plus the parent's spec.md, the validation reference documents the skip, the playbook states children are unbounded, and the template banner is correctly scoped. Four surfaces are silent about scope entirely: level-contract-resolver reads only warnChars and errorChars and drops appliesTo. The hook's resolveGoalBudget does the same and budgetState compares every packet, so both front ends emit packet_budget=over plus a warning claiming the slice is past the error tier for a document the validator passed. The playbook then tells the operator never to drop a criterion, which is the harmful action this false positive invites.

findings.text: The same pinned offer line means set a goal on plan and do not call the tool on resume
findings.detail: One literal is asserted in all four presentation files. Plan's set choice binds or sets; resume's set choice carries the objective into the brief and routes actual setting elsewhere, and resume asserts it never calls opencode_goal. The contract test locks the text and the allowed-tool list but nothing locks the semantics, so a third meaning could appear unnoticed.

findings.text: The plan workflow documents --runtime Pi, which is only valid because normalization lowercases first
findings.detail: The namespace pattern rejects uppercase, but the value is lowercased before the test, so the documented line works and reads as a typo. A reader cannot tell which reading holds without running it.

findings.text: The authoritative hub row names both flag spellings, and the three surfaces that get it wrong are downstream of it
findings.detail: The hub coverage row carries OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED as canonical and OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED as its alias. The correct pairing exists in the repository; the three surfaces that present the alias as primary are downstream of a hub that is right.

findings.text: Retrieval reaches the engine docs and the playbook but not the rule that checks the budget
findings.detail: The index carries the engine README, the plugin contract, the state-dir README, the set-string playbook, two feature catalogues and three CLI playbooks. It carries no entry for validation-rules.md section 12 or the goal template, so a search for the durable-budget rule finds the prose that describes it and not the rule that enforces it. paths[27] is a README inside the live state directory, tracked only by a gitignore negation.

findings.text: The workflow that decides to bind is the workflow that surfaces the budget false positive
findings.detail: bind is the one action that reports packet_budget. Plan routes any packet with a goal.md to bind, so the ring-3 workflow triggers the ring-1 scope bug at the moment the operator is being asked to adopt the packet as the directive.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: /goal resume reactivates three statuses in the plugin and two in both catalogues, while the core refuses two of them
findings.detail: Plugin resumeGoal passes allowedFrom ['paused','usage_limited','budget_limited'] and the transition map independently grants usage_limited->active and budget_limited->active. Both feature catalogues say resume reactivates only paused or usage_limited. The runtime-neutral core throws INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION unless status is paused. Three surfaces, three behaviours for one verb; nobody documents the core's stricter rule, and the core can never reach the two extra statuses because its VALID_STATUSES set is active|paused|completed|cleared.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: Two goal engines with incompatible status vocabularies and no mapping: completed vs complete, plus surface-specific cleared/blocked/usage_limited/budget_limited
findings.detail: Core statuses are active|paused|completed|cleared, documented in the engine README's injection sentence. Plugin statuses are active|paused|blocked|usage_limited|budget_limited|complete, documented in goal-opencode.md's argument-hint and the plugin catalogs/playbook. completed and complete name the same operator concept with different strings; cleared, blocked, usage_limited and budget_limited are each surface-specific with no cross-reference. bin/goal.cjs show prints status=completed where /goal show prints status=complete.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: CC-029 and its benchmark evidence rest on a constitutional rule file that no longer exists
findings.detail: A path .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/constitutional/goal-prompting-runtime-specific.md is cited as CC-029's constitutional routing authority in the playbook and in four benchmark record files including the JSON constitutionalRuleRel field. system-spec-kit has no constitutional/ directory and a repo-wide name search finds only the citations. Provenance INFERRED from a .git/lost-found object that once held the file's text (a runtime-specific rule about the /goal -> /opencode_goal rename). Settling action: restore the file or repoint the citations at the goal_prompting block of speckit-plan.yaml, which the sentence actually names.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: CL-007's evidence cites a command filename that does not exist (goal_opencode.md) while its quoted lines match the real hyphen file exactly
findings.detail: The playbook cites .opencode/commands/goal_opencode.md (underscore) four times, including 'Command file read confirmed ... exists', but the real file is goal-opencode.md. Every quoted line number and string (4 allowed-tools, 15 the state-free router sentence, 37 the never-reads-state sentence, 39 empty-arguments routing) matches the hyphen file exactly, so only the citation path is stale. The old spelling survives in deep-loop benchmark fixtures, consistent with a rename that left citations behind.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: CO-039 pins seven suites and 125 tests; the glob matches eight suites and this run reports 137/137
findings.detail: CO-039 says 'the 7 opencode-goal-*.test.cjs suites exist' and 'the focused suite passes 125/125'. Observed in this iteration: the glob matches 8 files and node --test .opencode/plugins/tests/opencode-goal-*.test.cjs reports tests 137 / pass 137 / fail 0. The playbook's pass criterion cannot be satisfied as written and nothing regenerates its numbers.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: plugins/README.md states a per-concern kill-switch rule that computes to the dead name SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED for goal
findings.detail: plugins/README.md gives the model as per-concern SYSTEM_<CONCERN>_DISABLED=1 with two SYSTEM_* examples, and lists OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED only among 'Legacy / plugin-specific aliases'. The true model is the inverse: goal is one of six CONCERN_CANONICAL concerns whose canonical name OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED is hand-set and test-pinned; OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED is its alias. Applying the printed rule yields SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED, the exact dead name in the operator's local hook-flags.env:25 (R1-F1, now downgraded). Three other rosters (hub table, shared README, ENV-REFERENCE) state the pair correctly.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: The root README promises injection on every turn; Cursor's only delivery is sessionStart
findings.detail: README.md:861 says the runtime injects the durable slice on every turn. True for OpenCode (transform), Pi (input) and Devin (SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit), but Cursor registers one delivery point, sessionStart, and the injection contract states beforeSubmitPrompt never delivers and stop never fires. retrieval-conventions.md:282 excludes the root README from both retrieval lanes, so nothing downstream corrects the reader.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: README's 'a parent goal' narrows the manifest's 'phase parents and top-level packets' scope
findings.detail: The public README sentence reads 'a parent goal warns past 3,000 characters and fails past 4,000' while the manifest scopes the budget to phase parents and top-level packets. A plain top-level packet is not a phase parent, so the README can read as excluding it. It is the only budget sentence outside the skill.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: PI-021 expects the legacy filename shape pi-<sha256>.json for fresh scoped state
findings.detail: PI-021's expected signals name two opaque pi-<sha256>.json files. A fresh scope writes <sha256-of-[workspace,runtime,sessionId]>.json; pi-<sessionDigest>.json is only the legacy adoption name used when the state dir is the workspace default. An operator validating the playbook by looking for pi-*.json after a fresh set finds none and could record a false FAIL.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: The word goal names four unrelated things in this repository and no document disambiguates them
findings.detail: (1) the session-goal system; (2) ordinary prose and feature labels (README Goal bullet, sk-git table column); (3) goal-file-manifest.txt, a deep-review scope manifest parsed as repo-relative paths, documented nowhere else in the live tree and unrelated to goal.md; (4) ClickUp product goals, whose card self-declares Capability status UNSUPPORTED. A grep for goal interleaves all four.

findings.ring: everything else that touches a goal
findings.text: CE-P03 explains injection-only as 'prompt surfaces do not receive the hook's native session id'; the hooks do, the command does not
findings.detail: CE-P03's causal clause misplaces the reason: cursor/goal-inject.mjs resolves payload.session_id with conversation_id fallback and both adapters write a turn touch, so the hooks have identity and write. What lacks identity is the command surface, which fails closed with UNSUPPORTED_SESSION_BINDING, as CU-027 states correctly. Extends the R1-F5 injection-only wording cluster to a second document.

findings.text: The save workflow's documented CLI log command is unrunnable as written, missing the scope flags that log requires
findings.detail: save.md instructs the append through three forms. The first, `node .opencode/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs log "<item> | <state> | <evidence>"`, omits --runtime/--session. log is not in actionsWithoutScope, so resolveGoalScope runs before dispatch and throws MISSING_RUNTIME/MISSING_SESSION_ID; goalOptions defaults only workspace to process.cwd(). The tool form (opencode_goal action log) is fine and the packet-log form on the same line is scope-exempt and complete (its action is in actionsWithoutScope and it passes --workspace anyway). The cell splitting is correct in both runLog and runPacketLog, so only the missing flags are wrong. Fix: add --runtime <r> --session <id> --workspace "$PWD", or route to packet-log.

corrections.text: resolveWorkspaceRoot is NOT dead code — the OpenCode plugin calls it
corrections.detail: Both twins are live in different implementations: the plugin uses goalSlice.resolveWorkspaceRoot, the core and Pi use resolveRepoRoot. Ring 1 could not see the plugin and read its own test-only reference as proof of death. The corrected finding is R2-F1: two live implementations of one walk, with the slice module claiming to be the single place the boundary is drawn.

corrections.text: The dead SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED line is local-only drift, not a shipped defect: git check-ignore confirms .opencode/hooks/hook-flags.env is ignored (.gitignore:287) and the committed hook-flags.env.example:25 carries the canonical OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED, which hook-flags.test.cjs:38 pins. What remains is the misleading rule statement in plugins/README.md:96-98 (R4-F6) that would still send an operator to the dead name.

resolvedQuestions.question: Who owns the hooks hub coverage row, and does the same table exist elsewhere that could drift?
resolvedQuestions.answer: The row is hand-maintained in .opencode/hooks/README.md (concern table :50, matrix :230-240, tree :135-142, sibling note :24) and restated independently in hooks/shared/README.md:88 and runtime/ENV-REFERENCE.md:83. The three agree today; nothing generates the hub table from hook-flags.cjs, whose test pins guard the resolver rather than the prose. The drift failure mode is already visible in plugins/README.md:96-98 (R4-F6).

resolvedQuestions.question: Is runtime/dist/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.js in step with the hand-written .ts carrying budgetApplies?
resolvedQuestions.answer: In step and freshness-gated. dist/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.js:853, :858, :863 carry isPhaseChildFolder and budgetApplies; dist/lib/templates/level-contract-resolver.js:192-199 carries the goalDurableBudget validation. validate.sh:26 runs the orchestrator from dist and validate.sh:29 consults cli/lib/dist-freshness.cjs, which compares source hashes and exits 69 on stale dist. Ring 3's finding therefore describes shipped behaviour.

resolvedQuestions.question: Do root instruction files and repo rules restate the budget, the resend rule or the offer in words that could drift from ring 3?
resolvedQuestions.answer: No. REPO RULES.md and all eleven repo-rules/*.md contain zero goal mentions. AGENTS.md:291-297 restates only the posture and delegates mechanics explicitly at :297; its posture lines match the slice module's frontmatter boundary and resendPending's hash semantics. Numbers, flags and channels appear only in README.md:861-866, where R4-F7 and R4-F8 find the two imprecisions.

resolvedQuestions.question: Do the feature catalogues and manual-testing playbooks describe the phase-child budget correctly and name the right disable flag?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Neither: the catalogues and playbooks do not describe the budget at all, so ring 3's contradiction stays confined to validation-rules.md and goal-set-string-playbook.md versus the hook. Six other defects were found in them instead (R4-F1, F3, F4, F5, F9, F11). The two playbooks that exercise the disable path (DV-022, CU-027 rollback) teach the alias OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED, which works but keeps the alias in circulation as the primary switch.
